lessons.title: láojià — may I trouble you (asking a favour)
lessons.gloss: may I trouble you (asking a favour)

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Mandarin for the owner of a lost item, then the Mandarin for to claim lost property.
láojià — "may I trouble you (asking a favour)".
láojià qù huǒchēzhàn zěnme zǒu — Excuse me, how do I get to the railway station?
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.

láojià is built from láo 'to tire' and jià 'a carriage', both inherited from Middle Chinese, law and kaeH (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'weary' and the second 'to ride'. The pair is usually explained as an old polite way of asking someone to trouble their carriage.
One more word for getting around.

lessons.title: bàituō — to ask a favour of someone
lessons.gloss: to ask a favour of someone

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Mandarin for to claim lost property, then the Mandarin for may I trouble you.
bàituō — "to ask a favour of someone".
bàituō nǐ bāng wǒ ná xíngli — Could you carry my luggage for me, please?
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.
bàituō is built from bài 'to bow' and tuō 'to entrust', both inherited from Middle Chinese, peajH and thak (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the second 'to entrust'.
One more word for getting around.

lessons.title: 多谢 (duōxiè) — many thanks; thanks a lot

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Mandarin for may I trouble you, then the Mandarin for to ask a favour of someone.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: 多谢

segments.text: 多谢 — duōxiè — "many thanks; thanks a lot".
多谢你我找到地图了 duōxiè nǐ wǒ zhǎodào dìtú le — Thanks so much: I've found my map.

多谢 (duōxiè) is built from 多 'many' and 谢 'to thank', both inherited from Middle Chinese, ta and zjaeH (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the second 'to decline'; the sense 'to thank' is not given there.
One more word for getting around.

Before the new one: say the Mandarin for to ask a favour of someone, then the Mandarin for thanks a lot.
gǎnjī — "to feel deeply grateful".
nǐ bāng le wǒ hěn duō wǒ hěn gǎnjī — You've helped me so much; I'm very grateful.
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.

gǎnjī is built from gǎn 'to be moved' and jī 'to surge', both inherited from Middle Chinese, komX and kek (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'to move' and the second as a rushing wave.
One more word for getting around.

lessons.title: 方法 (fāngfǎ) — a way to solve a problem; means
lessons.gloss: a way to solve a problem; means

blocks.title: You'll want to know: 方法

segments.text: 方法 — fāngfǎ — "a way to solve a problem; means".
找不到路的时候你有什么好方法 zhǎo bu dào lù de shíhou nǐ yǒu shénme hǎo fāngfǎ — When you can't find the way, what do you do?

方法 (fāngfǎ) is built from 方 'a technique' and 法 'a rule', both inherited from Middle Chinese, pjang and pjop (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first, among other senses, as an art or technique and the second 'a rule'.
One more word for getting around.
